endorsements.quote: Dataset statements should explicitly document how data were generated, which perspectives were excluded, and what assumptions shaped documentation practices.
Inclusion audits can assess whether marginalized diagnoses like DID are adequately represented and accurately characterized in training datasets.

unlisted_practices: Provide patients with pathways to challenge inaccuracies in their records.
Give patients meaningful input into how their data are used in research and algorithm development.
Allow patients to access their clinical notes, except where disclosure poses immediate safety risks.
Integrate validated dissociation screening tools and trauma measures into standard psychiatric intake protocols.
Dedicate psychiatric curriculum time to recognizing dissociative presentations.
Conduct regular diagnostic bias audits with structured decision-making tools in psychiatric practice.
Use inclusive, strengths-based, nonjudgmental language in clinical documentation.
Involve patients and communities in documentation design, education, and service planning.
Treat clinical data as ethically consequential infrastructure in AI governance.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective piece examining epistemic injustice in dissociative identity disorder documentation and arguing for data governance and documentation reforms to avoid algorithmic bias when training AI.
